name: Shop-painted structural steel (ISO 12944 protective paint system)
process: After welding, the welds are ground and faired and the whole lattice is abrasive blast-cleaned to Sa 2 1/2 (mill scale, rust and old coatings removed, only slight staining left). In the fabricator's shop it is sprayed with a two-coat protective system rated for a C2 environment with very high durability: an epoxy build coat of 125 um, then a polyurethane topcoat of 55 um, 180 um nominal dry film thickness in all. The topcoat carries the colour, a dark grey, and leaves the faint orange-peel texture of spray-applied paint. Bolted or site-welded joints are touched up after erection with the same system. The steel is seen only through its paint.

environment.text: The lattice is inside the heated Rotunda (ISO 12944-2 C1, heated interiors with clean air, steel corrosion at most 1.3 um a year), but it lies directly under the glazing, where condensation can form on cold nights: the system is therefore specified for the next category, C2 (unheated buildings and low-pollution atmospheres, 1.3-25 um a year). The condensation argument is this record's reasoning, not a measurement.

C1.source: World of Corrosion, 'ISO 12944 Coating Systems' (ISO 12944-2 C1 very low: heated interiors, offices, shops, schools; <= 1.3 um/year), https://worldofcorrosion.com/iso-12944.html

C2.source: World of Corrosion, 'ISO 12944 Coating Systems' (ISO 12944-2 C2 low: unheated buildings, rural areas; 1.3-25 um/year), https://worldofcorrosion.com/iso-12944.html

photograph: An even dark grey with a satin sheen and a faint spray orange peel.
Faired welds; the steel itself is never seen.

unverified.reason: F0 = ((n-1)/(n+1))^2 = 0.040 for a binder index n = 1.50. The refractive index of the polyurethane topcoat was not read from a source; organic binders lie near 1.5.
The topcoat's gloss level (ISO 2813, 60 degrees) was not specified by a source; a satin finish is the usual architectural choice but no value was read.
No measured amplitude or wavelength of spray orange peel on a polyurethane topcoat was read.
The condensation risk under the glazing is argued, not measured; Light and Studio could measure the glass's inner-face temperature against the dew point at the reference moments.
